identity.title: WSM: Decay-Free Learning Rate Schedule via Checkpoint Merging for LLM Pre-training

problem.claim: The paper addresses decay-free learning-rate scheduling for LLM pre-training, using checkpoint merging to retain competitive performance without a traditional decay phase.

contributions.claim: Introduces Warmup-Stable and Merge (WSM), a framework formally connecting learning-rate decay with model merging.
Provides a unified theoretical foundation for emulating cosine, linear, and inverse-square-root decay through principled model averaging, compatible with diverse optimizers.
Identifies merge duration as more influential on performance than checkpoint interval or merge quantity.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish WSM by establishing a formal connection between learning-rate decay and checkpoint merging, and by representing multiple decay strategies as model-averaging schemes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that, with high-quality annealing data, WSM outperforms WSD across multiple benchmarks: +3.5% on MATH, +2.9% on HumanEval, and +5.5% on MMLU-Pro.
The authors report that WSM’s performance advantages also extend to supervised fine-tuning scenarios.
The authors report from extensive experiments that merge duration is the most critical factor affecting model performance, exceeding checkpoint interval and merge quantity in importance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Decay-free learning-rate approaches and model merging are presented as promising ways to avoid traditional learning-rate decay while maintaining competitive performance.
WSM is introduced as a framework formally relating learning-rate decay to checkpoint merging.
The framework is described as emulating cosine, linear, and inverse-square-root decay via model averaging across optimization methods.
Experiments identify merge duration as the key merge-design factor and report benchmark gains over WSD with high-quality annealing data.
The reported advantages extend to supervised fine-tuning.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a formal mechanism to several concrete decay strategies, then reports which implementation factor matters most empirically.

lessons.interpretation: A strong abstract can align a general conceptual claim with both its scope and a focused sensitivity finding.
lessons.application: When presenting a general training framework, enumerate the covered strategy variants and identify the design variable that experiments report as most consequential.
lessons.exception: Avoid this framing when the work does not support broad theoretical coverage or comparative factor analysis.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify model sizes, training budgets, baseline implementation details, statistical variation, or benchmark protocols.
The meaning and construction of “high-quality annealing data” are unspecified, limiting interpretation of the reported gains.
The abstract does not provide the formal derivation or conditions underlying the claimed equivalence between decay and merging.
